newsitem.title: DUBAI: Iranians march to protest at German court verdict.
newsitem.headline: Iranians march to protest at German court verdict.

text.p: Chanting crowds marched in towns and cities across Iran on Monday to protest against a German court ruling accusing top Iranian leaders of ordering political killings in Berlin, state-run Tehran radio said.

Marchers, echoing condemnation of Thursday's ruling by Iranian leaders, branded it a legally baseless and political move taken by the Berlin court under pressure from the United States and "international Zionism".

The radio broadcast reports from the demonstrations held in a dozen towns and cities ranging from Iran's Caspian coast in the north to the centre and West of the country and stretching to the Gulf coast.

In Tehran, large numbers of bazaar traders held a protest meeting at a mosque and condemned the court's accusations as "yet another plot serving the goals of Arrogance (West) against the Islamic Republic's system of government", it said.
The radio broadcast special programmes denouncing the ruling that Tehran leaders ordered the 1992 killings of four Iranian Kurdish opposition figures in Berlin.
Iran has repeatedly denied any role in the killings which it blames on infighting between opposition groups.

The radio repeatedly carried remarks by President Akbar Hashemi Rafsanjani blasting the verdict as provoked by Israel and the United States -- Iran's arch-enemies -- but adding that a diplomatic row over the ruling was a "passing storm".

The official Iranian news agency IRNA said a large number of veterans disabled by Iraqi chemical attacks in the 1980-88 war between the two neighbours would march on Wednesday to the German embassy in Tehran.
The war veterans would also protest against German firms which provided toxic chemicals to Iraq, IRNA said.
Iran has said court proceedings would begin shortly against 24 German companies accused of having helped Iraq produce chemical weapons during its war with Iran.
On Sunday, hundreds of thousands of angry Iranians called for Germany's downfall in a protest at the embassy, the second since Friday.
Iran has responded to the withdrawal of all European Union ambassadors except Greece's by announcing it would pull its envoys out of those countries in return.
Germany made clear at the weekend it would seek to avoid stepping up the dispute with Iran over the ruling.

Bonn officials say privately that, behind the scenes, Iran has signalled it does not wish to raise the temperature in the diplomatic stand-off with a country which, until recently, was its biggest trade partner and friend in the West.
